why: The Coverr and Mixkit roller/wall-painting clips were all amateur or cheesy (smiling couples, tattooed DIY, garish green and yellow paint, hard cuts), so I picked the most premium modern-finishing interior instead: a loft room with a full-height oak-panelled wall, leather sling chairs, an arched steel lamp and a band of dusk-lit windows. The grade is muted and warm, with oak close to the brass #C9A87C, ivory walls and a near-black floor, so it sits in the same warm, low-key family as the build sunset poster under the #0E0A06 overlays. No people, logos, text or watermarks. Source 1080p cropped to 1536x864 (x 192, y 0) so a magazine cover at the bottom of the frame stays out, then scaled to 1280x720. The camera is a slow, decelerating crane, so the loop is a ping-pong of source frames 118-215 (4.9-9.0 s): 8.09 s, 194 frames, with no crossfade ghosting. The turnarounds fall where the motion is ~0.4 px/frame. Seam diff 1.07 vs a median frame step of 0.57, which is I-frame grain only. The lamp sits at x~0.52, so focusX 0.52 keeps it and the oak wall in a mobile crop. Poster is output frame 24
